returned_textual_content: # API Quick-start tutorial This tutorial introduces you to the Solidatus API and takes you through steps to ingest content into a model via the API. {% hint style="warning" %} This tutorial requires the curl command line utility. {% endhint %} There are four actions covered in this tutorial: 1\) [Request an API token](#request-an-api-token) 2\) [Create an empty model](#create-a-model) 3\) [Add content to the model](#update-the-model) 4\) [Next steps](file:///Users/peterwoodford/Documents/GitHub/solidatus-docs/build/html/api/tutorials/quick-start.html#next-steps) ## Request an API token All calls to the Solidatus API endpoint need to be authenticated using an API token. > 1. Go to the API tokens page. This can be accessed by clicking on your initials in the top right of the [the navigation bar](/the-user-interface/the-navigation-bar), selecting *Account*, and scrolling down to the *API tokens* section. > 2. Enter a name for your new token > 3. Select the “Create model” and “View model” scopes > 4. Click “Create token” > 5. The token will then be displayed for you to copy and use in subsequent commands in the Authorisation header, as shown {% hint style="danger" %} Make sure you copy the token right away because you will NOT be able to see it again later. If you lose the token, you will need to create a new one. {% endhint %} [Read more about API authentication.](/api-documentation/api-overview/api-authentication) ## Create an empty model * In the curl command below: * Replace the `PASTE_THE_API_TOKEN_HERE` with your API token from above. * Replace `https://solidatus-host` with your Solidatus URL. * Execute the command to create an empty model called “My model”. **Request** ``` curl --header "Content-Type: application/json" \ --header "Authorization: Bearer PASTE_THE_API_TOKEN_HERE" \ --request POST \ --data '{"name": "My model"}' \ https://solidatus-host/api/v1/models ``` **Response** ``` { "id": "5f06f5a716bd8b0001dc2a03", "name": "My model", "description": "", "type": "LineageModel", "referenceModelType": null, "owner": { "id": "54d0b14018d86418ccfdc157", "name": "Joe Bloggs" } } ``` You will use the returned model `id` (e.g. `5f06f5a716bd8b0001dc2a03`) in the following command to update the model. ## Add content to the model There are many model update commands available to edit an existing model (for a full list of available commands, see [model update commands](/api-documentation/api-actions/api-use-the-api)). This example uses the *ReplaceModel* command to insert entities using the [Solidatus JSON format](/api-documentation/api-actions/solidatus-json-format). * First, copy and paste the below JSON to a file called `body.json` and save it. ``` { "cmds": [ { "cmd": "ReplaceModel", "model": { "entities": { "1": { "name": "My layer1", "properties": {}, "children": ["2"] }, "2": { "name": "My object1", "properties": {}, "children": ["3"] }, "3": { "name": "My source attribute", "properties": {} }, "4": { "name": "My layer2", "properties": {}, "children": ["5"] }, "5": { "name": "My object2", "properties": {}, "children": ["6"] }, "6": { "name": "My target attribute", "properties": {} } }, "transitions": { "3:6": { "source": "3", "target": "6", "properties": {} } }, "roots": [ "1", "4" ] } , "comparator": { "path": true } } ], "commit": true, "commitMessage": "Merge in new model data" } ``` * From the directory containing the body.json file, execute the command to update the model. **Request** ``` curl -X POST \ --header "Content-Type: application/json" \ --header "Authorization: Bearer PASTE_YOUR_API_TOKEN_HERE" \ --data @body.json \ https://solidatus-url/api/v1/models/PASTE_MODEL_ID_HERE/update ``` **Response** ``` { "changeset": [], "ids": { "4": "e6499251-438a-4e01-970d-3fa32b8fb020", "3": "0e20ec3c-9e73-44c4-98eb-418d87764261", "2": "bbe17ed4-d6f0-4c3a-8724-c58b74ca85d0", "3:6": "2fb57996-cb0f-4966-9144-75c8c966f94d", "6": "39408d89-60df-4e35-ad1b-6dbb06b70232", "5": "dd7474f5-1a17-42eb-b45b-7e79fdf6bff6", "1": "ccf0b81b-5b6c-4ee0-8b81-076471de157c" }, "errors": [], "revisionId": "67fd1027e37484e1ad33b385", "draftId": null, "draftRevisionId": null } ``` * Go to the model list in the [Model Browser](/the-user-interface/models-ui/model-browser), open it, and you will see the resulting entities. ## Next steps You can find more information about interacting with models using the API [here](/api-documentation/api-actions). A comprehensive developer reference for our REST API can be found through the help menu in your Solidatus instance.
